source_text: Hoc lumen nobis uitae salutaris exortum, hoc in reparationem hominis natum de Dei patris procuratione ac miseratione praesidium. magi primi ab orientali parte uenientes et stella eius duce Iudaeorum regem palam praescia praedicatione quaerentes, adferentes etiam munera testificata omnibus inquisitione monstrarunt. et ne aliquibus quis ille esset esset absconsum, inuentum puerum procidentes genibus adorarunt, sicut testificatur euangelium dicens: cum autem Iesus natus esset in Bethleem Iudae in diebus Herodis regis, ecce magi ab oriente uenerunt in Hierosolymam dicentes: ubi ost qui natus est rex Iudaeorum. uidimus enim stellam eius in orientem et uenimus adorare eum. testificantes scilicet ueritatem de eo etiam stellam sibi signum atque indicium natiuitatis ipsius esse monstratam, qua indice natum illum magis praedicantibus et adfirmantibus et Hierosolymis crederetur. Simeon quoque iustus qui in caecitate constitutus diuino monitu audierat se non ante moriturum quam uidisset Christum, cum in templum omni populo praesente infantem secum mater inferret, in spiritu Christum natum esse sensit, acceptum in manus puerum uidit et benedicens Deum in conspectu et auditu omnium dixit: nunc dimittis seruum tuum Domine secundum uerbum tuum in pace quoniam uiderunt oculi mei salutare tuum. Simeon quod caecus audierat euidenti ueritate perfectum est, et ueritatem quam accepto lumine uiderat benedicendo palam Deum populo praedicabat. ad hoc enim uiderat, ut referret, ut reuelatione sua quod Christus. natus fuisset ostenderet et perfidi populi initia prima incredulitatis instrueret.
thought_title: The light of salvation shown to the Magi and Simeon
orientation: The author is showing how Christ's birth was publicly testified from the very beginning, first by the Magi and then by Simeon in the temple.
pass_a_gloss: This light of saving life has arisen for us, this protection for the repair of man has been born from the care and compassion of God the Father. The Magi first, coming from the eastern region and with his star as guide, openly seeking the king of the Jews with foreknowing proclamation, bringing also gifts testified to all by their inquiry, pointed him out. And lest it be hidden from any who that one was, falling on their knees they worshipped the found boy, as the gospel testifies saying: But when Jesus had been born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold Magi from the east came into Jerusalem saying: Where is he who has been born king of the Jews? For we have seen his star in the east and have come to worship him. Testifying namely the truth about him, that also a star had been shown to them as a sign and indication of his birth, by which indicator the one born was believed by the Magi proclaiming and affirming and in Jerusalem. Simeon also the righteous, who established in blindness had heard by divine warning that he would not die before he had seen Christ, when the mother brought the infant with her into the temple with all the people present, perceived in spirit that Christ had been born, received the boy into his hands, saw him, and blessing God in the sight and hearing of all said: Now you dismiss your servant, Lord, according to your word in peace, because my eyes have seen your salvation. What blind Simeon had heard was fulfilled with evident truth, and the truth which he had seen when light was received he was proclaiming openly to the people by blessing God. For this he had seen, so that he might report it, so that by his revelation he might show that Christ had been born and might instruct the first beginnings of unbelief of the faithless people.

choices.why: Keeps the literal sense of 'reparatio' as repair or restoration, matching the source's concrete image of fixing what was broken.
Renders the adjective 'praescius' literally as 'foreknowing' to preserve the idea that their proclamation was informed by prior knowledge.
Keeps the literal 'constitutus' as 'established' to preserve the odd phrasing of the source, which emphasizes Simeon's settled state of blindness.
Renders both 'initia' and 'prima' literally to preserve the emphatic doubling in the source.
Uses the glossary term 'faithlessness' for 'perfidia' family, rendering the adjective 'perfidus' as 'faithless' to match the fixed glossary.

pass_b_english: This light of saving life has arisen for us; this protection was born for the repair of man through the care and compassion of God the Father. The Magi, coming first from the eastern region and seeking the king of the Jews openly with foreknowing proclamation, led by his star, pointed him out to everyone by bringing gifts and testifying through their inquiry. And so that it might not be hidden from anyone who he was, when they found the child they fell forward on their knees and worshipped him, as the Gospel testifies, saying: "Now after Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, Magi from the east came to Jerusalem, saying, 'Where is he who has been born king of the Jews? For we saw his star in the east and have come to worship him'" (Matthew 2:1-2). They were testifying to the truth about him, and also that the star had been shown to them as a sign and indicator of his birth, so that by that indicator the Magi might proclaim and affirm that he was born, and it might be believed in Jerusalem. Simeon also, a righteous man established in blindness, had heard by divine warning that he would not die before he had seen Christ. When the mother brought the infant with her into the temple in the presence of all the people, he perceived in the Spirit that Christ was born, took the child into his hands, saw him, and blessing God in the sight and hearing of all said: "Now you dismiss your servant, Lord, according to your word, in peace, because my eyes have seen your salvation" (Luke 2:29-30). What Simeon had heard while blind was fulfilled with evident truth, and the truth that he had seen when he received light he proclaimed openly to the people, blessing God. For this reason he had seen, so that he might report it, so that by his revelation he might show that Christ had been born and instruct the first beginnings of unbelief of the faithless people.
